title: OpenMock
description: Schema for an OpenMock document — an open format for defining API mocks in a single YAML file. A document declares a list of named, type-tagged servers, each carrying its own operations. Validates the envelope strictly while allowing arbitrary YAML bodies and messages.

openmock.description: The OpenMock format version this document targets (SemVer).

servers.description: The mock servers this document describes. Each server is named, carries one protocol type, and holds its own operations; a document may declare several servers of the same type.

items.$comment: Discriminated on type so a malformed server is validated against the one shape it means, not reported as failing all four. Server-name uniqueness is a spec-level load-time rule (§3.6) — JSON Schema cannot compare values across array items.

serverName.description: The server's name: how normalized requests address it. Unique across the servers list (a spec-level load-time rule).

serverPort.description: Optional default port hint for implementations serving this server over a network. A hint only: it never affects routing, matching, or rendering, and engines MAY override it. See docs/serving.md.

httpServer.description: An HTTP mock server: a named group of method+path operations.

grpcServer.description: A gRPC mock server: a named group of service+rpc operations, optionally carrying its compiled protobuf schema.

descriptorSet.description: Path, resolved relative to the document, to a serialized google.protobuf.FileDescriptorSet covering the services this server mocks. Implementations MAY ignore it; it never changes matching or responses.

items.$comment: Discriminated on the call type: server-streaming operations use messages, everything else is unary and uses message.

graphqlServer.description: A GraphQL mock server: a named group of operationType+operationName operations, optionally carrying its SDL schema.

schema.description: Path, resolved relative to the document, to a GraphQL schema in SDL covering the operations this server mocks. Implementations MAY ignore it; it never changes matching or responses.

websocketServer.description: A WebSocket mock server: a named group of connection-path operations.

path.description: Absolute path template; {name} segments capture path parameters.

service.description: Fully-qualified gRPC service name, matched case-sensitively.

type.description: The RPC's call type. unary is the default; write it explicitly for clarity.

service.description: Fully-qualified gRPC service name, matched case-sensitively.

type.description: Server-streaming call type; required, never inferred from response shape.

operationType.description: The GraphQL operation type. query is the default; subscriptions are not part of v0.2.

operationName.description: The GraphQL operation name this route answers, matched case-sensitively.

path.description: Path template the connection is established against; {name} segments capture path parameters.

name.description: Identifier for the scenario, unique within its operation.

summary.description: Optional human-oriented description of the scenario's intent. Non-normative.

httpWhen.description: Condition under which an HTTP scenario applies. All declared facets must match. Omitting when makes the scenario the default fallback.

grpcWhen.description: Condition under which a gRPC scenario applies. All declared facets must match. Omitting when makes the scenario the default fallback.

graphqlWhen.description: Condition under which a GraphQL scenario applies. All declared facets must match. Omitting when makes the scenario the default fallback.

websocketWhen.description: Condition under which a WebSocket scenario applies. params/query/headers match the connection-scoped values fixed at establishment; message matches the individual inbound message. All declared facets must match. Omitting when makes the scenario the default fallback.

callsMatcher.description: Matches the operation's call counter: an exact positive integer, or an object with inclusive min/max bounds (at least one required). `n` is shorthand for {min: n, max: n}.

body.description: The response body as native YAML/JSON — any object, array, or scalar. Intentionally unconstrained.
body.$comment: Arbitrary bodies are allowed by design; only the envelope is validated strictly.

error.description: gRPC status message accompanying a non-OK status.

metadata.description: Initial response metadata (headers), sent before the response message.

trailers.description: Trailing response metadata (trailers), sent with the final status.

message.description: The unary response message as native YAML/JSON. Intentionally unconstrained.
message.$comment: Arbitrary messages are allowed by design; only the envelope is validated strictly.

else.$comment: A unary call yields either a response message or an error status, never both.

error.description: gRPC status message accompanying a non-OK status.

metadata.description: Initial response metadata (headers), sent before the first message.

trailers.description: Trailing response metadata (trailers), sent with the final status.

delay.description: Delay before the first message, in milliseconds.

messages.description: Ordered response messages, emitted first to last. May be combined with a non-OK status (stream that fails mid-way).

graphqlResponse.$comment: A GraphQL response carries data, errors, or both (a partial response).

data.description: The response's data payload as native YAML/JSON. Intentionally unconstrained.
data.$comment: Arbitrary data is allowed by design; only the envelope is validated strictly.

errors.description: GraphQL errors, in order. May be combined with data (a partial response).

extensions.description: Top-level response extensions: free-form, machine-readable data the GraphQL spec permits alongside data/errors.

graphqlError.description: A GraphQL error object, per the GraphQL specification: message plus optional locations, path, and extensions.

path.description: Path to the response field the error concerns: field names (strings) and list indices (integers).

extensions.description: Free-form, machine-readable error details. Intentionally unconstrained.

websocketResponse.$comment: A WebSocket response carries reply messages, a close, or both. An empty messages list with no close deliberately ignores the inbound message.

messages.description: Ordered reply messages as native YAML/JSON, emitted first to last. MAY be empty (ignore the inbound message). Intentionally unconstrained items.

close.description: Close the connection after the last reply message.

delay.description: Delay before the first reply message (or the close), in milliseconds.

grpcStatus.description: A canonical gRPC status code name.

stringMap.description: A map of string keys to string values.

existsMatcher.description: Presence matcher: true asserts the target is present (any value), false asserts it is absent.

patternMatcher.description: Pattern matcher: an RE2 pattern matched against the target's entire canonical string form (implicitly anchored). A pattern that is not valid RE2 makes the document invalid.

matcherMap.description: A when-facet map: each value is a string (exact match on canonical string form) or a matcher object ({exists: bool} | {pattern: RE2}). At least one key — an empty facet map is not a constraint.

payloadMatcher.description: body/message facet: a map of dotted paths to strings or matcher objects, or a single string matching the whole payload by its canonical string form.

queryMatcherMap.description: Query facet: each value is a non-empty list matched against the parameter's full occurrence sequence exactly — same order, same count; elements are strings or pattern matchers. Alternatively an exists matcher asserts the parameter's presence or absence. There is no string form. At least one key — an empty facet map is not a constraint.

headerMap.description: Response headers: each value is a string, or a non-empty list of strings emitted as one field line per item, in order (for headers that cannot be comma-joined, like Set-Cookie).
